Governor Abbott Announces Over $20 Million In Career Training Grants Across Texas

Governor Abbott Announces Over $20 Million In Career Training Grants Across Texas

October 12, 2026 | Austin, Texas 
      |

Press Release

Governor Greg Abbott today announced 84 
Jobs and Education for Texans (JET)
 grants totaling over $20 million have been awarded to Texas public junior, state, and technical colleges; school districts; and open-enrollment charter schools.

The JET grants, awarded through the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC), will help schools buy equipment to start or improve career and technical education (CTE) training programs that lead to high-demand careers. In the first year alone, the new equipment will help train more than 7,400 students.

“Students deserve a clear and affordable path to high-paying careers,” said Governor Abbott. “Through more than $20 million in career training grants, Texas students will have the opportunity to earn licenses, certificates, or college degrees that lead to high-wage jobs. By investing in our students today, we are building a stronger Texas for generations to come.”

“A skilled workforce is essential to the success of Texas businesses and the strength of our economy,” said TWC Chairman Joe Esparza. “With more than $20 million in funding for career and technical education programs, TWC is investing the skills young Texans need to build their careers and ensure employers have the talent pipeline they need to thrive.”

The 2026 JET grants will be used to purchase and install equipment at the following public junior, technical, and state colleges:

Alamo College (Northwest Vista College): a $375,000 grant to train 300 students as data scientists.

Angelina Jr College District: a $305,116 grant to train 100 students as registered nurses.

Brazosport College: a $222,509 grant to train 80 students as registered nurses.

Coastal Bend College: a $350,987 grant to train 38 students as radiologic technologists and technicians.

College of the Mainland: a $355,686 grant to train 146 students as registered nurses.

Collin College: a $346,697 grant to train 120 students as welders.

El Paso County Community College District: a $283,385 grant to train 12 students as electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians.

Galveston College: a $293,886 grant to train 320 students as welders.

Grayson College: a $375,000 grant to train 75 students as HVAC mechanics and installers.

Lamar State College Orange: a $97,026 grant to train 80 students as emergency medical technicians.

Lamar State College Port Arthur: a $141,907 grant to train 10 students as welders.

Lee College: a $97,964 grant to train 15 students as engineering technologists and technicians.

Lone Star College: a $49,667 grant to train 120 students as engineering technologists and technicians.

Midland College: a $319,043 grant to train 420 students as automotive service technicians and mechanics.

Through funding provided by the Texas Legislature, TWC uses JET grants to defray start-up costs to develop career and technical education programs for eligible applicants. Equipment funded through JET grants must be used to train students for jobs in high-demand occupations.

TWC will release the 2027 JET grant Request For Applications (RFA) later this fall. Texas public junior, state, and technical colleges, school districts, open-enrollment charter schools, the Texas Juvenile Justice Department (TJJD), and Probation Departments may apply.

Once posted, the complete JET application packet can be downloaded from the TWC Procurement Portal website. To receive notifications about this and other procurement opportunities, interested parties can
